title: Vermigli, Musculus, Placeus: firm assent that draws fiducia, hope, charity
source_text: XIII. Apud Petrum Martyrem fides definitur, Firmus certusque animi assensus verbis Dei, a spiritu divino afflatus ad salutem credentium. Postea vero exponit quid per assensum firmum intelligat, nempe, Illum qui tantarum sit virium & efficaciae, ut secum trahat affectum fiduciae, spei, charitatis, & omnia tandem bona opera, ut praesentis vitae infirmitas patitur. Locor. commun. Classe 3. cap. 4. num. 5. Musculus similiter fidem definit, Constantem assensum cordis ad ea quae vel narrantur, vel promittuntur verbo. Loco de Fide, Sectione 1. Et eodem redit definitio fidei quae legitur apud Josuam Placeum, Professorem Salmuriensem doctissimum & acutissimum, cui Fides est Tenax & efficax persuasio veritatis eorum quae verbo Dei nobis revelata sunt, speciatim vero promissionum remissionis peccatorum & vitae aeternae nobis per Christum factae. Thesibus de Justificatione Thesi 36.
pass_a_gloss: In Peter Martyr faith is defined as a Firm and sure assent of the mind to the words of God, breathed by the divine Spirit unto the salvation of believers. But afterward he explains what he understands by firm assent, namely, That which is of such powers and efficacy that it draws with it the affection of trust, of hope, of charity, and at length all good works, as the weakness of the present life suffers. Common Places, Class 3, ch. 4, num. 5. Musculus similarly defines faith as a Constant assent of the heart to those things which are either narrated or promised by the word. Place on Faith, Section 1. And to the same comes the definition of faith which is read in Joshua de la Place, most learned and acute Professor of Saumur, for whom Faith is a Tenacious and efficacious persuasion of the truth of those things which have been revealed to us by the word of God, but especially of the promises of remission of sins and of eternal life made to us through Christ. Theses on Justification, Thesis 36.
pass_b_english: Vermigli: firm sure assent to God’s words, Spirit-breathed unto salvation.
‘Firm’ means efficacy that pulls fiducia, hope, charity, and good works along (as this life allows).
Musculus: constant heart-assent to what the word narrates or promises.
Placeus (Saumur): tenacious efficacious persuasion — especially remission and eternal-life promises in Christ.
